title: The Burnham plan vs the triple lock
subject: The fiscal saving from the Burnham plan for the State Pension (from April 2030, rises of at least the higher of CPI and 2.5%, topped up to keep the 2029-30 value relative to earnings) against the triple lock to 2039-40: its expected value over paths of prices and earnings and its range across reweightings, the saving on the OBR central and OBR-wedge paths, what it would have saved had it started in 2012 or 2017, and which households have less income, from full PolicyEngine UK runs.

burnham_2030.description: The Burnham plan: from April 2030 the basic and new State Pension rise by at least the higher of CPI and 2.5%, and by more where needed to keep their 2029-30 value relative to earnings; scored against the triple lock (current law), which applies to every earlier April under both rules.

burnham_since_2012.description: The plan's rule replayed on published inputs from April 2012 (the same path from any April 2012 to 2015), against the triple lock as paid; the dashboard's 'If the Burnham plan had started earlier' section.

burnham_since_2017.description: The plan's rule replayed on published inputs from April 2017 (the same path from any April 2016 to 2018), against the triple lock as paid; the scenario envelope's last-decade replay.

earnings_link_instead_of_triple_lock.description: The Resolution Foundation's approximation of the plan: the basic and new State Pension uprated in line with earnings instead of by the triple lock, with no CPI or 2.5% floor; scored against the triple lock.

pe_estimates.label: Expected gross saving, Burnham plan vs triple lock, 2031-32
pe_estimates.sign_basis: results.json prints the saving as a positive number of pounds billion (gross: the fall in basic and new State Pension spending); benefit_cost_change is stated positive = increase in spending, so a saving is negative

conditions.measure: gross: the fall in basic and new State Pension spending
